characterized_levers.name: Technical Feasibility Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: Demonstrating technical feasibility impacts policy. Immediate: Demonstrators built → Systemic: 15% increased policy traction due to concrete evidence → Strategic: Enhanced credibility in procurement negotiations.
options: Focus demonstrator efforts on a single, highly secure authentication method, such as FIDO2, on a mainstream Android device.
Develop demonstrators for both FIDO2 on GrapheneOS and a browser-based fallback, accepting slightly longer development timelines.
Explore passwordless authentication via blockchain-anchored identity and decentralized identifiers (DIDs) alongside FIDO2 and browser-based fallback demonstrators.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Technical Risk vs. Scope. Weakness: The options don't explicitly address the cost implications of each demonstrator approach.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on demonstrating technical feasibility to impact policy, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of the technical demonstrators on policy traction, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to demonstrator development.
characterized_levers.description: The Technical Feasibility Strategy aims to demonstrate that platform-neutral and fallback-capable digital identity solutions are technically viable. It controls the scope and focus of technical demonstrators, influencing the credibility and persuasiveness of the project's technical evidence. Success is measured by the robustness and security of the demonstrators, their alignment with open standards, and their ability to function in simulated or real-world environments. Key metrics include successful authentication rates, security audit results, and positive feedback from technical stakeholders.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: This lever strongly synergizes with the Procurement Influence Strategy (f1c0d856-0cfc-4def-ab68-c58bb8b17551). Credible technical demonstrators provide concrete evidence to support procurement requirements for platform neutrality and fallback access, making the advocacy efforts more effective.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: This lever can conflict with the EU Standards Engagement Strategy (2e9016aa-8563-447e-a5e0-0e146f4ebad3). Focusing too narrowly on specific technical solutions in the demonstrators might limit the project's ability to adapt to evolving EU standards and interoperability requirements.

characterized_levers.name: Policy Advocacy Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: Policy advocacy shapes procurement. Immediate: Policy proposals submitted → Systemic: 20% greater likelihood of influencing AltID requirements → Strategic: Increased adoption of platform-neutral standards.
options: Focus advocacy on continuity of service and supplier concentration risks, avoiding direct privacy arguments.
Balance continuity arguments with privacy and democratic accountability concerns, broadening the coalition.
Prioritize open-source governance and community-led development models for digital identity, framing platform neutrality as a public good.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Political Risk vs. Coalition Size. Weakness: The options don't consider the potential for regulatory capture by incumbent vendors.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on policy advocacy shaping procurement, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of policy advocacy on influencing AltID requirements, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to advocacy focus.
characterized_levers.description: The Policy Advocacy Strategy focuses on shaping the policy landscape to favor platform-neutral and fallback-capable digital identity solutions. It controls the messaging and arguments used to influence policymakers and regulators. The objective is to secure formal policy commitments and procurement requirements that promote these solutions. Success is measured by the inclusion of relevant language in policy documents, regulations, and procurement specifications, as well as positive engagement from key stakeholders.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: This lever works in synergy with the Coalition Building Strategy (1731ad9a-c471-40de-9b90-12f23721aebd). A broader coalition, encompassing diverse perspectives, strengthens the advocacy efforts and increases the likelihood of influencing policy decisions in favor of platform neutrality.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: This lever can conflict with the Technical Feasibility Strategy (bd43cd39-f2f0-4358-9f5b-e4dbfdccc474). Overly ambitious policy goals, such as prioritizing open-source governance, may be difficult to achieve if the technical demonstrators cannot provide sufficient evidence of feasibility and security.

characterized_levers.name: Coalition Building Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: Coalition strength amplifies advocacy. Immediate: Stakeholder engagement increased → Systemic: 30% stronger advocacy position in procurement discussions → Strategic: Greater political pressure for platform neutrality.
options: Build a narrow coalition focused on security experts and contingency-planning stakeholders.
Expand the coalition to include civil-society organizations, privacy advocates, and academic researchers.
Actively recruit dissenting voices from within the MitID operator and Digitaliseringsstyrelsen to foster internal debate.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Speed vs. Breadth of Support. Weakness: The options fail to address the potential for conflicting priorities within the coalition.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on coalition building to amplify advocacy, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of coalition strength on advocacy position, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to coalition composition.
characterized_levers.description: The Coalition Building Strategy aims to create a strong, diverse alliance of stakeholders who support platform-neutral digital identity in Denmark. It controls the breadth and depth of support for the project's goals, influencing political pressure and advocacy effectiveness. Success is measured by the size and diversity of the coalition, the level of engagement from its members, and its ability to influence policy discussions. Key metrics include the number of participating organizations, the frequency of coalition meetings, and the impact of coalition statements on public discourse.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: This lever strongly enhances the Policy Advocacy Strategy (80b177d0-c67e-4bc2-bd50-3f49b815e633). A broader, more engaged coalition provides a stronger voice when advocating for policy changes and engaging with Digitaliseringsstyrelsen. It also supports the Procurement Influence Strategy.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: A broad coalition may dilute the focus of the Technical Feasibility Strategy (bd43cd39-f2f0-4358-9f5b-e4dbfdccc474) if diverse stakeholders pull the project in conflicting directions. Balancing technical rigor with broader political considerations requires careful management and prioritization.

characterized_levers.name: Procurement Influence Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: Procurement influence drives adoption. Immediate: Platform-neutral language included in procurement documents → Systemic: 25% faster scaling through mandated supplier diversity → Strategic: Reduced long-term dependency on Apple and Google.
options: Focus on including general language about supplier concentration risk in AltID procurement documents.
Advocate for specific requirements for platform-neutral access and certified fallback authentication paths.
Propose a 'digital sovereignty bonus' in procurement scoring, rewarding vendors who demonstrably reduce platform dependency.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Specificity vs. Implementability. Weakness: The options don't account for the potential for vendors to game the procurement process.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on procurement influence driving adoption, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of procurement influence on scaling, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to procurement language.
characterized_levers.description: The Procurement Influence Strategy focuses on incorporating platform-neutrality and fallback access requirements into Danish digital identity procurement processes, particularly AltID. It controls the specificity and strength of these requirements, driving adoption of supplier-neutral solutions. Success is measured by the inclusion of relevant language in procurement documents and the resulting reduction in platform dependency. Key metrics include the number of procurement documents influenced and the diversity of vendors selected.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: This lever works in synergy with the Technical Feasibility Strategy (bd43cd39-f2f0-4358-9f5b-e4dbfdccc474). Credible technical demonstrators and feasibility reports provide evidence to support the inclusion of platform-neutral requirements in procurement documents. It also benefits from the Coalition Building Strategy.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: This strategy may conflict with the EU Standards Engagement Strategy (2e9016aa-8563-447e-a5e0-0e146f4ebad3) if Danish-specific procurement requirements diverge significantly from broader European standards. This could create friction and limit interoperability, requiring careful alignment.

characterized_levers.name: EU Standards Engagement Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: EU standards engagement creates broader impact. Immediate: Input provided to relevant EU bodies → Systemic: 10% increased alignment with European Digital Identity Wallet requirements → Strategic: Enhanced interoperability and reduced lock-in across Europe.
options: Monitor relevant EU bodies and technical working groups, providing occasional input on interoperability.
Actively engage with EU bodies, advocating for platform-neutral access and certified fallback mechanisms in eIDAS2 and related standards.
Champion a 'sovereign identity sandbox' within the EU Digital Identity Wallet framework to test and validate platform-neutral authentication models.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Resource Allocation vs. Scope of Influence. Weakness: The options don't address the potential for EU standards to be influenced by large platform vendors.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on EU standards engagement creating broader impact, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of EU standards engagement on alignment with European Digital Identity Wallet requirements, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to EU engagement strategies.
characterized_levers.description: The EU Standards Engagement Strategy focuses on influencing European digital identity standards to promote platform-neutrality and fallback authentication mechanisms. It involves actively participating in relevant EU bodies and technical working groups related to the European Digital Identity Wallet framework. The objective is to align Danish advocacy with broader European requirements on interoperability, portability, resilience, and reduced platform lock-in. Success is measured by the inclusion of platform-neutrality or fallback access language in relevant European Digital Identity Wallet materials.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: This lever strongly synergizes with the Policy Advocacy Strategy (80b177d0-c67e-4bc2-bd50-3f49b815e633). EU standards engagement provides a broader platform for advocating the policy changes necessary for platform-neutrality. It also enhances the Procurement Influence Strategy (f1c0d856-0cfc-4def-ab68-c58bb8b17551) by creating external pressure.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: This lever can conflict with the Technical Feasibility Strategy (bd43cd39-f2f0-4358-9f5b-e4dbfdccc474). Over-ambitious EU engagement might outpace the project's technical capacity to demonstrate viable alternatives. It also competes for resources with the Coalition Building Strategy (1731ad9a-c471-40de-9b90-12f23721aebd), potentially diverting focus from domestic support.
